## Observation
In run 44232977541 at dd72b461814, the "sweep (windows)" job (134562252974) failed `tests/unit/test_unique_cache_writes.py::test_concurrent_cursor_writes_never_report_a_write_error`:

`AssertionError: a concurrent cursor write was silently dropped: ['reconcile_cursor_write_error']` (`tests/unit/test_unique_cache_writes.py:182`)

The test races 2 threads through `rebar.review_bot.reconcile._write_cursor`, with a barrier on the replace step. It failed in 1 of 3 Windows sweeps (passed in runs 44211859981, 44141097601 and 44253676986).

## Root cause (evidence)
`_write_cursor` (`src/rebar/review_bot/reconcile.py:100-108`) publishes through `rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write`, whose last step is a bare `os.replace(tmp, path)` (`src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py:119`). On Windows `os.replace` is `MoveFileEx(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)`, which fails with `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (WinError 5, raised as `PermissionError` errno 13) while another handle holds the target or another rename onto it is in flight; POSIX `rename(2)` never fails that way. The same seam failed the same way in the scheduled Windows sweeps at `b4e0d01b649` (run 43820680079 and its siblings, logs read 2026-11-18): `test_unique_cache_writes.py::test_two_concurrent_writers_to_one_target_both_publish` recorded `PermissionError(13, 'Access is denied')`; `test_mcp_gate_async.py::test_follower_start_does_not_reclobber_the_leaders_index_record` logged `PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied: '...\.rebar\gate_runs\....tmp' -> ...` from `atomic_write` (`src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:92`); `reconciler/apply/test_bridge_state_atomic_write_concurrency.py` logged `peer_confirmations: could not persist ... (PermissionError(13, 'Access is denied'))` through `atomic_write` (`src/rebar/reconciler/sidecar_transactions.py:68`). Sites that call `os.replace`/`Path.replace` directly fail the same way: `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_verdict_cache.py:217` (`test_completion_verdict_cache.py::test_concurrent_persist_for_same_criterion_loses_no_writer`, `{'A': 0, 'B': 1}`) and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/checkpoints.py:138` (`test_plan_review.py::test_concurrent_save_checkpoint_same_digest_loses_no_writer`, `{'B': False}`). The cursor test captures only event names, so its own failure carried no kwargs.

## Approach
Fix the class at the shared publish step. Add `replace_with_retry(src, dst)` to `rebar._store.fsutil`: on Windows (`os.name == "nt"`, read once into a module constant the tests can patch) it retries `os.replace` on `PermissionError` with a short backoff (10 ms doubling, capped at 100 ms) until a 2 s deadline, then re-raises the last error; on POSIX it is exactly `os.replace` with no retry. Every other `OSError` propagates at once on both platforms. A bounded retry fits because the Windows failure is transient by nature (the competing rename or handle finishes within milliseconds) and the callers already treat a final failure as before. Route these publish sites through it: `fsutil.atomic_write` (`fsutil.py:119`; covers the cursor, gate runs and bridge-state sidecars), `completion_verdict_cache.py:217`, `plan_review/checkpoints.py:138`, `reconciler/binding_repository.py:79`, `reconciler/apply_planning.py:346`, `reconciler/get_rotation.py:105`, `reconciler/last_pass.py:285`, `llm/evals/fixture_admission.py:437`. No config key, env var or flag is added.

Portability: the retry branch only runs where `os.name == "nt"`; it uses only `os.replace` and `time.sleep`.

The barrier tests intercept the replace step; a retried replace would wait on the barrier a second time and hang. Make each barrier one-shot per thread (the first publish attempt waits, retries pass through), which still forces the two writers to collide.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py` (helper + `atomic_write`), and the 7 call sites listed above.
- `tests/unit/test_fsutil_replace_retry.py` (new): helper unit tests.
- `tests/unit/test_unique_cache_writes.py` (one-shot barrier; cursor test records `(name, kwargs)` so any failure prints the error text), `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_verdict_cache.py`, `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` (one-shot barrier on `os.replace`).
- `.github/windows-sweep-deselect/file-locks.args`: remove the 5 lines this fixes (`test_two_concurrent_writers_to_one_target_both_publish`, `test_concurrent_persist_for_same_criterion_loses_no_writer`, `test_concurrent_save_checkpoint_same_digest_loses_no_writer`, `test_peer_confirmations_distinct_concurrent_saves_are_merged`, `test_follower_start_does_not_reclobber_the_leaders_index_record`). The rest of that file stays with charitable-tyrannical-hydra.

## Testing
- Helper, with the Windows constant patched on: 2 `PermissionError`s then success publishes after 3 calls; a persistent `PermissionError` re-raises after the deadline (patched to a short value); `FileNotFoundError` is never retried. With it patched off (POSIX): `PermissionError` propagates after exactly 1 call.
- The existing concurrency tests still pass on POSIX with one-shot barriers. `make verify` passes.
- Windows: 3 consecutive dispatched `sweep (windows)` runs on main after the merge.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The failing OSError at the shared publish seam is recorded on this ticket with its type, errno and winerror and the Windows run ids above, and the cursor test records emitted event kwargs.
- [x] `make verify` passes on the change, including the new `test_fsutil_replace_retry.py` tests.
- [x] `test_concurrent_cursor_writes_never_report_a_write_error` and the 5 tests removed from `file-locks.args` pass in 3 consecutive `sweep (windows)` runs on main after the fix, and the job concludes `success` in each (run ids recorded in a comment).
